The '''cancelled German release of SWCCG''' is a planned German-language Star Wars CCG printing that was later cancelled. Surviving artifacts are 1998 German-market magazine advertisements and a Modern Graphics German two-player rulebook.

On 11 December 1995 Diane Tennant reported in ''The Virginian-Pilot'' that Decipher would produce the game "in six languages over two years from the plainest of storefronts on Granby Street." The same story said translating the cards "into German, French, Dutch, Spanish and Italian may be tricky," and that "A bigger problem might be the German language itself, which requires a good many more words and letters to get a point across than does English, and space, while vast in the universe, is limited on a playing card."<ref name="pilot">Diane Tennant, ''House of Cards'', ''The Virginian-Pilot'', Daily Break p. E1 (11 December 1995; TAG 9512090048). Google's public index of the Virginia Tech electronic copy still extracts those sentences: [https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Translating+the+cards+into+German%2C+French%2C+Dutch%2C+Spanish+and+Italian%22 named languages]; [https://www.google.com/search?q=%22produced+in+six+languages+over+two+years%22+Decipher+Granby six languages]. That copy at scholar.lib.vt.edu returned HTTP 410 Gone on 9 October 2026. The Wayback Machine had no capture of the article URL.</ref> On 16 February 1997 the sister paper ''Daily Press'' quoted Decipher vice president of sales Ross Campbell saying the game "also will be translated into six languages this year."<ref name="dailypress">[https://www.dailypress.com/1997/02/16/norfolk-games-company-finds-the-force/ Norfolk games company finds the Force], ''Daily Press'' (16 February 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009181930/https://www.dailypress.com/1997/02/16/norfolk-games-company-finds-the-force/ Wayback, 9 October 2026].</ref> Encyclopedia 3.2, under Other Foreign Language Releases, records additional language releases planned beyond the Japanese sets. Those further languages were not released.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p.201 (Other Foreign Language Releases). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Wayback, 9 October 2026]. Collecting hub: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ starwarsccg.org/collecting/].</ref>

In April 2022 Andy Talaga showed 1998 German-market magazine issues advertising a forthcoming German Premiere edition. Those issue numbers match ''Offizielles Star Wars Magazin'' #8–#11 (Miracle Images / OZ Verlag: 14 January, 15 April, 15 July, and 10 October 1998). He said the German edition was supposed to be the first European language release, that the campaign ran in two issues, and that later issues dropped it.<ref name="boardmatt-jp">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1tdmHYND4xc Star Wars CCG - Japanese Card Overview], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (3 April 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-1tdmHYND4xc Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="oswm">[https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-8/ Offizielles Star Wars Magazin #8], Jedi-Bibliothek (14 January 1998). [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-9/ #9] (15 April 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ #10] (15 July 1998); [https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ #11] (10 October 1998). Preserved copies: [https://web.archive.org/web/20241223104413/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-10/ Wayback #10, 23 December 2024]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009164751/https://jedi-bibliothek.de/datenbank/ausgabe/offizielles-star-wars-magazin-11/ Wayback #11, 9 October 2026].</ref> He said Decipher outsourced European language support to Queens Games, which he placed in Munich, and that they pulled the contract after Japanese sales.<ref name="boardmatt-jp" />

In May 2022 Andy showed a 1998 German two-player rulebook printed by Modern Graphics, with Decipher logos and an all-German interior. Two-player sets sold in Germany were English [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game|Waddingtons]] kits. The booklet was prepared so players who could not read English could learn the game.<ref name="boardmatt-col">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4dR5MIPH4h4 Star Wars CCG - Most Interesting and Strangest Things in Our Collections with Special Guest Andy], BoardMatt, guest Andy Talaga (29 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-4dR5MIPH4h4 Internet Archive].</ref>

Decipher's May 1999 product library lists the English Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set and does not list a German SKU.<ref name="library">[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game : The Expansions], Decipher.com product library (archive, 4 May 1999).</ref> Language editions of SWCCG are on [[Translations of SWCCG]].
